segments: Let me say in December or January 1980, I
was reassigned from the Pentagon to RAF Fentwaters
in East Suffolk, England.
At that time, Fentwaters was the largest
tactical fighter wing in the world.
It was supposed to two geographically
separated bases in England, four operating
locations
in Germany and two standby locations in
Germany.
The concept of operation was that should the
Eastern Bloc countries come through the
Boulder Gap and into Germany.
The A-10s at Fentwaters would pick up lock,
stock, and barrel and move to Germany and go
kill
armor, and the base would be backfilled with
strike aircraft.
We even had pre-positioned weapons for it.
A very strange event occurred in December of
that year, 1980.
The night of December 25th, the morning of
December 26th, our security police were
doing
their routine patrols on the base when the
patrol at RAF Woodbridge saw what he thought
with a dying aircraft in the forest out from
the East Gate.
They called us the control center.
They checked with all the pertinent
authorities and they came back.
Nothing's flying, nothing in the air,
nothing reported dying.
So a small group of three security policemen
went into the forest to investigate.
What they saw from the gate was multiple
lights, red lights, blue lights, flashing
lights.
They approached an object, metallic in shape,
triangular, about nine feet on a side,
sitting on the
equivalent of a pedestal.
What happened from then on, the rest of the
evening, we're not really sure because their
memory has been altered.
They had a very unusual experience.
There's probably more than an hour of lost
time.
They did come back to the base all, how
should I say, concerned and upset.
Most of the police didn't want to talk about
it.
It was kind of hush-hush.
They did make a minor entry in the police blotters.
It requires to be.
Most of us, the senior officers, thought,
well, there had to be an explanation and
didn't
get too excited.
Two nights later, I was at the end of the
year, sort of a Christmas party, recognition
dinner for the officers in the combat
support group.
It was a covered-dish family affair.
And we just finished eating when the on-duty
police lieutenant came in, just white as a
sheet.
And he said to the base commander and I, "It's
back."
Of course, we said, "What's back?"
And he said, "The UFO."
And we just looked at each other.
We did believe him.
Well, my boss had to make a presentation and
give a speech or two, so he fell on me to
go investigate.
I went home, changed clothes, and gathered
up a small group of people, including the
disaster preparedness, NCO, and had them
bring a ganger kind and a camera along.
We went out into the forest, and he took me
to a site, three indentations in the ground,
equal distance apart, about an inch and a
half to two inches deep, and said, "Here's
where the object was seen two nights before."
Lo and behold, when we put the ganger
counter down, we got radiation readings were
nine
to ten times higher than background
radiation.
Rub marks on the trees.
Obviously, something had happened there.
Looking up through the trees, which by the
way were very mature, of course, at the pines,
you could see an opening in the canopy
directly above the broken branches, though
something
had gone up or come down.
While we're there milling around trying to
figure out what was going on or what had
happened,
one of the members of the party said, "Look,
there's a strange red light out there."
Looking through the forest, we saw an object,
glowing object, oval, like this, probably a
little larger than a basketball.
It had a dark center, and it appeared to be
winking.
It was moving from side to side and shedding
the equivalent of molten metal.
Something was dripping off it.
We watched the object for probably a minute
or two.
It came into the forest in the field.
It moved through the trees horizontally, bobbing
up and down occasionally to miss branches.
It came towards us at one point and then receded
back out into the farmer's field, which was
to the east of us.
We moved up to the fence line to get a
better look at it, and I could see the glow
off the windows in the farmer's house until
the house was on fire.
The right was blowing.
Oh, just like a fire.
I was quite concerned for the office in the
house.
The whole time we could see the Orford Nest
lighthouse off to the right.
It was a white light.
The object finally exploded like fireworks
into multiple white objects and they
disappeared.
Whoa.
We went out into the field and searched
around to see if we could find any evidence
of whatever was coming off the object
compared to shedding something.
We found nothing except evidence of cattle.
While we were looking around, we decided to
go further out into the far field to get a
better look in the sky.
In front of the party, I don't remember who
it was, that looked at the north.
There were multiple objects in the sky.
They were elliptical, multicolored, more or
five of them.
They turned in a half-moon shape.
They were moving in synchronization together,
making sharp angular turns.
We just stood there in awe.
I had taken my small pocket recorder along,
so I was reporting most of this information.
I called the command post on the radio.
By the way, we were having trouble with the
radio.
They were really acting up.
And asked them to have the eastern radar,
who had air defense for that sector, look in
the sky and that was their place.
They came back and said, "They don't find
anything."
I said, "Does anybody with any of the radar
see anything?"
And I was told no.
Well, lo and behold, several years later I
found out that the air traffic controllers
in the Pentwater's tire did see the object.
It came close to the air traffic control
tire.
It was glowing red.
It crossed their 60-mile scope in seconds,
twice, went out into the area we were and
they saw it descend into the force.
Well, this didn't come out until several
years later.
I also found out that the eastern radar had
picked up a blip or two at the same time.
That didn't come out until later because it
was a misunderstanding on the dates.
So, I wish I'd known that then, but I didn't.
We continued on watching the objects in the
sky and saw two to the side.
One of the objects at the south, standing
down, I would say beams alight, sort of like
laser beams, into Woodbridge base and Bentwater
base, primarily into Bentwater base.
They landed somewhere in or near the weapons
storage area.
I could hear a lot of chatter on the police
radios, talking back and forth about what
was going on, what they saw.
It was really puzzling.
The object to the south came overhead,
directly overhead, very high speed, stopped
3 or 4,000 feet of elevation.
10 times we put them to laser feet, right by
our feet, about 10 feet away from us.
We all just stood there in awe.
We had a message, a method of communication,
a warning, something lethal.
We were just trying to move.
Just as suddenly as the object refused, it
disappeared.
The object went back to the south.
We stayed out there for several hours,
trying to figure out what was going on.
There was no interest on the part of the
command post.
Nobody would say anything.
They didn't know anything, supposedly.
So, after three or four hours, we returned
back to the base.
I took my tape and played it for several of
the senior officers, including the wing
commander.
We took it to the 3rd Air Force headquarters,
the staff meeting, and they played my tape.
And the two-star general said to my boss, "Well,"
he said, "Is Halt credible?"
He said, "Yes."
So, the general turned to the staff and said,
"Well, what do we do?"
Nobody answered.
So, the general said, "Well, it happened off
the base.
Therefore, it must be a British affair."
So, my boss came back and gave me the tape
back, and I said, "What do I do?"
He said, "We'll get with the liaison officer
for the RAF."
He was in Wales on holiday.
I had to wait a week or so.
So, when he came back, he and I kind of agonized,
and he said, "Write a memo."
So, I wrote a memo.
I kind of cleaned it up and made it sanitized
just a little bit, assuming it would go to
the M.O.D., Ministry of Defense, and I would
get an inquiry, and somebody would come
investigate it.
So, I took a few days turned into weeks,
turned into months.
Actually, I was quite happy.
I really didn't want to be involved.
In fact, the whole time we were out in the
forest investigating, I kept thinking, "Why
did I get involved?"
Nobody's going to ever believe this.
How do I explain this?
This is not exactly career enhancing.
Well, to this day, I don't know what
happened.
I do know that there was some strange
phenomena, some things we couldn't
understand.
The objects we saw were obviously intelligently
controlled.
They went at high speed, faster than
anything we know.
I don't have the answer.
I certainly wish I knew more.
The three young airmen that were out
initially to investigate have never been the
same.
That's all I'm going to say on that.
They had chromatic experience, and they're
lightbulking, I guess, is the best way to
put it.
I have never been officially debriefed,
which is interesting.
I've had a lot of inquiries and talked to a
lot of high-level people.
Again, no answer.
I wish I knew more.
